The Contractor may include more than one species on the same PAR if those species are treated in the same location with the same pesticide (See Attachments – BMDO Pesticide Application Record (PAR)). As part of the PARs process, the Contractor shall provide onsite spot weather while applying the herbicide. Mixing Methods: All mixing shall be done to label, BLM, and state policies and requirements. This can include secondary containers, specific measurements and calibrations, spill containment and cleanup, and ensuring mix sites are in correct locations. The applicators and Contractor shall ensure they follow these policies. Quality Assurance and Quality Control Methods: The Contractor shall furnish equipment to monitor and ensure evenly spaced, straight, regular, and complete coverage of all areas included in the Contract. The Contractor shall ensure the correct spray rate is applied and that there is quality control in place to ensure the ground coverage is complete and accurate. Both the Contractor and the Government will conduct tests as operations progress to determine uniformity of application. The BLM COR/PI may utilize randomly placed drift cards. The Contractor shall provide to the Government: A written plan explaining how the Contractor will determine uniformity of

ntract. The contractor shall be responsible for purchasing, safely transporting, storing and disposal of the herbicide as follows: Herbicide *A BLM-approved Imazapic at 8 fluid ounces per acre. Adjuvants *BLM approved surfactant compatible with the application type, active ingredient, and applied at the rate identified on product’s labels. **See section 4.4 for the Chemical and Adjuvant options available for use within this contract. The contractor shall ensure the application of the herbicide meets all label specifications. The contractor shall be responsible for cleanup of accidental spills, following proper handling and storage precautions, and ensuring proper exposure control and personal protection is provided, as defined by the Herbicides’ and Adjuvants’ herbicide Safety Data Sheets. The contractor shall comply with all Federal, State, and Local regulations. Required Equipment Navigation: For ground applications, a GPS unit is required for tracking and data collection. The Contractor shall provide GPS tracks for any location where herbicide is applied. The system shall be sufficiently sensitive to provide an accuracy of ± 15ft in either the WGS84 or NAD83 datum. ponsible for giving the contractor any special instructions or guidance necessary to complete delivery as required by the contract. The COR and/or PI does not have the authority to modify or in any way amend the terms of this contract. Safety The Contractor is responsible for providing a safety plan that identifies a point of contact in the event of any accident. The plan should include names and emergency phone numbers for personnel and facilities to contact in case an emergency warrants such actions. The plan should also include a description of on-site emergency procedures to follow in case of an accident. The plan should identify the insurance company providing coverage and the pertinent group coverage number. In addition to being responsible for the safety of their employees, the contractor is also responsible for providing for the safety of the public during operations. This includes compliance with all OSHA and State of Nevada regulations for the use of equipment. Any hazards that would pose a danger to Contractor, Contractor’s personnel, the public or operating equipment should be identified, mitigated and/or avoided by the Contractor and brought to the Government representative’s attention. Purpose The purpose of this contract is to design and implement a complete digital exhibit experience— including digital interpretive content, exhibit concept development, and audio-visual integration—for a series of interconnected historical exhibits at the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit—Innovation Center. The exhibits shall translate the Government's approved artistic and interpretive vision into engaging, technically reliable, museum-quality visitor experiences. 2. Background The Innovation Center is developing a suite of digital and AV-enhanced exhibits depicting historical figures, events, and narratives connected to the site. GENERAL 1.1 Scope: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service) requires routine road grading and snow-removal services at Rice Lake National Wildlife Refuge (Refuge), located at 36289 State Highway 65, McGregor, Minnesota 55760. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, equipment, vehicles, transportation, fuel, materials, supplies, permits, and other resources necessary to perform the services described in this statement of work (SOW) and each authorized Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) call. Services may include: - Routine grading of existing gravel roads - Snow plowing of Refuge roads, access roads, and parking lots; - Wing plowing to move accumulated snow away from roadways and shoulders; and - Application of salt and/or sand at the headquarters parking lot and maintenance shop area. The work is limited to the locations and service items identified in Section 7 and on the attached maps. 1.2 Nature of the Requirement Road grading under this BPA is limited to routine maintenance of existing gravel roads. ctor shall be responsible for damage caused by its personnel or equipment. Damage to roads, signs, gates, culverts, buildings, vehicles, utilities, vegetation, or other property shall be reported immediately. 2 CONTRACTOR FURNISHED EQUIPMENT, MATERIALS, AND SUPPLIES 2.1 General The Contractor shall furnish equipment of the type, size, and condition necessary to perform the ordered services safely and effectively without causing unnecessary damage to Refuge roads, shoulders, parking lots, structures, vegetation, or other property. All equipment shall be properly maintained and operated in accordance with applicable laws, manufacturer requirements, and accepted industry practices. 2.2 Road-Grading Equipment The Contractor shall furnish grading equipment capable of smoothing the existing gravel surface, eliminating minor surface irregularities, restoring the existing road crown, and redistributing existing gravel without unnecessarily removing surface material from the roadway. 2.3 Snow-Removal Equipment The Contractor shall furnish snowplowing and wing-plowing equipment capable of safely clearing the designated roads, access areas, and parking lots while maintaining adequate travel width. GENERAL INFORMATION A. Introduction and Background The U. S. Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Science Center, Seattle Field Office (SFO), requests laboratory services for tree ring samples collected from paleoseismological and landslide studies in the Pacific Northwest. Paleoseismologists and geologists conduct studies of active fault zones and lands

e Pacific Northwest. Paleoseismologists and geologists conduct studies of active fault zones and landslides throughout the Pacific Northwest. An integral part of these studies are tree ring analyses to determine precise ages of past earthquakes and coseismically- triggered landslides. The USGS does not have the in-house capabilities to provide proper sample collection, preparation, processing, and final analysis. C. Scope The purpose of the laboratory work is to provide support services and the preparation and processing of wood samples for tree ring and isotope analyses. We anticipate needing analyses on up to 20 tree samples (core or slabs containing ring series of hundreds of rings). The criteria for acceptance of services shall be finished wood preparation, dissection of rings, radiocarbon and isotope analyses, and preparation and analysis of individual growth increments and analysis results for cross-dating analysis. The methods now also use oxygen isotopes as a means for cross-dating samples in addition to radiocarbon and traditional dendrochrologic techniques, resulting in a multi-proxy, cross-validated geochronologic process.
